items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: me and this boy they called Lonnie Johnson now, we called him Rooster at home, but we'd play on Saturday evening on a big store gallery

ctx.x: Now before that in Raceland would you make any money?

Oh yeah we'd make, like, me and this boy they called Lonnie Johnson now, we called him Rooster at home, but we'd play on Saturday evening on a big store gallery you see, and put our hat down and all the people that's playing put money in our hat see, we didn't have no siren or nothing like that. But when we got through, that Saturday and that Saturday night, that Saturday evening and that Saturday night, we ain't gonna have enough money to lend us all that next week. See? Yeah.
Just play that one day and you'd have enough to make it all.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Come out and did an act with us on guitar.

ctx.x: Well, that's what Johnny Wiggs says, and he heard Oliver in person. He said he was just playing his old style that he played before he went to normal.

Oh. Mm-hmm. Well... Lonnie never makes records with Lonnie because he left here way before me. Did you ever see him? Did you ever run across him after he'd become better known in yourself? Did you? Did you ever get together together? Yeah, I never really did. Did you ever play with anybody? Did you ever play in the same group together? Well, I'm going to tell you what happened.
